chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

One day, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to his companions: “Accursed is every wealth that is not purified, and accursed is every body that is not purified, even if only once in every forty days.”

So it was said: “O Messenger of Allah, as for the zakat of wealth, we have come to know it; then what is the zakat of bodies?” He صلى الله عليه وآله said to them: “That they be afflicted by an affliction.”

He عليه السلام said: Then the faces of those who heard that from him changed. So when he صلى الله عليه وآله saw that their colors had changed, he said to them: “Do you know what I meant by my statement?” They said: “No, O Messenger of Allah.”

He صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Rather, it is that a man is scratched by a scratch, struck by a mishap, stumbles a stumble, falls ill with an illness, is pricked by a thorn, and whatever resembles this,” until he mentioned in his hadith even the twitching of the eye.

key_terms.آفَةٍ: An affliction or harmful occurrence that strikes a person.
key_terms.اخْتِلَاجَ الْعَيْنِ: The twitching or involuntary movement of the eye, mentioned as part of minor afflictions.
key_terms.النَّكْبَةَ: A mishap or setback that befalls someone.
key_terms.الْمَرْضَةَ: An illness or sickness affecting the body.
key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْأَجْسَادِ: The purification of bodies, explained here as afflictions that befall a person.
key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْمَالِ: The prescribed purification due on wealth.
key_terms.مَلْعُونٌ: Accursed; used here as a warning regarding what is left without purification.
key_terms.يُزَكَّى: Is purified; in context, both wealth and the body have a form of purification.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the purification of the body through afflictions?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that just as wealth is purified through zakat, the human body is also given a kind of purification through minor afflictions and hardships. It reframes ordinary pains, illness, and small injuries as spiritually meaningful trials rather than mere misfortunes.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘One day Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to his<sup>saww</sup> companions: ‘Accursed is every wealth not purified! Accursed is everybody not purified, and even though it be once every forty days’.

So it was said to himsaww, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! As for the Zakāt (purification) of the wealth, so we have recognised it, so what is the purification (Zakāt) of the bodies?’ So hesaww said: ‘Being hit by the afflictions’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So the faces of those who heard that from him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, changed. So when he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> saw their colours to have changed, said to them: ‘Do you all know what I<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> meant by my<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> words?’ They said, ‘No, O Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>!’

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Afflictions of the man. He gets scratched by the scratch, and he has misfortune of a calamity, and he stumbles by tripping, and he gets sick by an illness, and he complains of the complaints (aches and pains), and whatever resembles this’, to the extent that he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> mentioned in his<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> Hadeeth, soreness of the eyes’.
en.sarwar: 26. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqa from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah one day said to his companions, ‘Condemned is every property that is not purified by paying al- Zakat (charity), condemned is the body that is not purified once in every forty days.’

He was then asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we know how property is purified, but what is al-Zakat (purification) of the bodies?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘It is the suffering of the body from certain forms of trouble.’

The narrator has said that the faces of those who heard it changed and when he noticed the change in their faces he asked them, ‘Did you understand what I meant by what I just said?’ They said, ‘No, O Messenger of Allah.’

He then said, ‘What I meant was that a man suffers a scratch or a set back, a slip, or illness, or is pricked by a spike or such other things.’ In his Hadith he also mentioned even sourness in the eyes.”
